claims.fact: Assistant gave a basic slow cooker yogurt recipe: heat 1/2 gallon milk on low 2-3 hours to 180°F–185°F (82°C–85°C), cool to 110°F–120°F (43°C–49°C), add 1/4 cup plain yogurt with live cultures, incubate 8-12 hours, then refrigerate.
claims.why: Directly provides procedural guidance for slow-cooker outcomes (yogurt in a slow cooker), including key temperatures and times.

claims.fact: Assistant said using a thermometer is highly recommended (but not strictly necessary) for yogurt milk heating to 180°F–185°F (82°C–85°C), and without a thermometer to heat 2-3 hours until simmering/boiling signs appear, then cool to 110°F–120°F (43°C–49°C) before adding starter.
claims.why: Offers advice about process control (temperature monitoring) that can affect slow-cooker results.

claims.fact: Assistant gave cashew-based slow cooker yogurt techniques: rinse 1 cup cashews; soak at least 4 hours or overnight; drain/rinse and soak again 4 hours or overnight; blend with 1/2 cup fresh water about 2 minutes; strain through cheesecloth/nut milk bag/fine-mesh sieve; chill at least 2 hours; use low heat to prevent scorching; incubate 8-12 hours; use vegan yogurt starter or probiotic powder.
claims.why: Includes detailed prep ratios, soak/blend/strain steps, timing, and equipment recommendations that strongly affect slow-cooker yogurt consistency.

claims.fact: Assistant restated a cashew process: soak 1 cup cashews at least 4 hours or overnight; blend with 1/2 cup fresh water about 2 minutes; strain; adjust cashews-to-water ratio for thickness; blend time affects consistency.
claims.why: Adds additional/confirming procedural details about consistency drivers (ratio, blend time, straining).

claims.fact: Assistant advised on straining cashew mixture tools for smooth consistency: cheesecloth, nut milk bag, or fine-mesh sieve; suggested squeezing to extract liquid; noted nut milk bag may be effective but can be pricey; fine-mesh sieve may be easier but can leave a slightly grainy texture; emphasized using clean/sanitized straining tool to prevent contamination.
claims.why: Provides direct guidance on straining method selection and technique, which directly affects texture/results.
